Why Sony Interactive Entertainment?

Sony Interactive Entertainment isn’t just the Best Place to Play — it’s also the Best Place to Work. Sony Interactive Entertainment (SIE) is the company behind the PlayStation brand. As a subsidiary of Sony Group Corporation, we’re part of a proud legacy of innovation and excellence. SIE is a dynamic technology company, delivering cutting-edge hardware and network services to more than 100 million people and an entertainment leader, home to some of the most beloved and recognizable intellectual properties (IP) in the world. Our role at SIE is to create and nurture the experiences under the PlayStation brand, a name synonymous with entertainment excellence and creativity.

 

What We Do
Sony Interactive Entertainment is the company behind PlayStation. We build tools, and experiences used by players and development teams across the PlayStation ecosystem.
Our team develops and maintains a multi-platform application framework that helps internal teams build rich PlayStation user experiences. The framework combines React Native, native platform integration, reusable UI components, SDK tooling, and developer documentation.

Are You Looking For A Challenge?
We are looking for a Software Engineer to help develop, maintain, and improve the application framework powering PlayStation user experiences across multiple platforms. You will work across JavaScript/TypeScript, native platform integration, C++, build systems, and SDK packaging.
The ideal candidate has strong software engineering fundamentals, real interest in framework and runtime work, and experience building reusable software such as SDKs, libraries, native modules, or cross-platform developer. Experience with React Native or Apple platforms such as iOS or macOS is a strong plus.

What You Will Be Doing
Implement, debug, and maintain application framework features across JavaScript/TypeScript and native layers.
Build and improve developer-facing APIs, native modules, framework components, and integration paths used by application teams.
Contribute to native framework code in C++.
Improve framework integration with React Native and native platform services.
Improve SDK packaging, framework templates, sample apps, documentation, and integration guides so partner teams can adopt framework capabilities with less support.
Debug issues across JavaScript, native code, build tooling, runtimes, and CI.
Maintain backward compatibility and clear versioning expectations for framework APIs.
Add tests, validation notes, and sample coverage for framework changes.
Collaborate with senior engineers, product teams, UI teams, and application teams to clarify requirements and land maintainable solutions.
Participate in code reviews and technical design discussions, with an emphasis on correctness, maintainability, performance, and developer experience.
What We Are Looking For
B.S. in Computer Science or equivalent practical experience.
2-5+ years of professional software development experience.
Experience building libraries, SDKs, frameworks, developer tooling, native modules, or other reusable engineering platforms.
Strong JavaScript or TypeScript experience.
Solid C++ fundamentals, including memory ownership, API boundaries, build/debug workflows, and performance-aware implementation.
Ability to debug across layers: JavaScript, native platform code, build systems, runtime logs, and CI output.
Strong API design judgment, including compatibility, versioning, error handling, documentation, and testability.
Comfort working in a large codebase with existing patterns and platform constraints.
Clear written communication for design notes, PR descriptions, validation results, and developer documentation.
Bonus Qualifications
Familiarity with React Native.
Experience with cross-platform SDKs or frameworks across iOS, macOS, Android, Linux, game console, or desktop platforms.
Experience writing high-performance or ABI-conscious C++ code.
Familiarity with CMake, Conan, CocoaPods, Gradle, Maven, npm, or other package and build distribution systems.
Experience with CI/CD systems such as Jenkins.
Experience building native UI components, focus/input systems, accessibility surfaces, performance instrumentation, or test harnesses.
Experience working with application teams as framework consumers and translating integration pain into reusable framework improvements.
 

At SIE, we consider several factors when setting each role’s base pay range, including the competitive benchmarking data for the market and geographic location.

Please note that the base pay range may vary in line with our hybrid working policy and individual base pay will be determined based on job-related factors which may include knowledge, skills, experience, and location. 

In addition, this role is eligible for SIE’s top-tier benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, matching 401(k), paid time off, wellness program and coveted employee discounts for Sony products. This role also may be eligible for a bonus package. Click here to learn more.

 

The estimated base pay range for this role is listed below.

$137,300 - $205,900 USD

Please note, Sony Interactive Entertainment conducts background checks at the offer stage for all new employees (which may include criminal background checks for some roles) and will need to process personal information to support these checks.

Please refer to our Candidate Privacy Notice for more information about what personal information we collect, how we use it, who we share it with, and your data protection rights.

Equal Opportunity Statement:

Sony is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All persons will receive consideration for employment without regard to gender (including gender identity, gender expression and gender reassignment), race (including colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin), religion or belief, marital or civil partnership status, disability, age, sexual orientation, pregnancy, maternity or parental status, trade union membership or membership in any other legally protected category.

We strive to create an inclusive environment, empower employees and embrace diversity. We encourage everyone to respond. 

Sony Interactive Entertainment is a Fair Chance employer and qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records will be considered for employment.

# Sony Play Station: Interview Briefing

This briefing prepares you for an interview for the Software Engineer role on Sony Interactive Entertainment's application framework team, which builds the multi-platform tooling (React Native, native integration, C++, SDKs) that powers PlayStation user experiences. Below is a synthesis of company news, business performance, tech stack context, culture signals, and role-specific details to help you speak knowledgeably and ask sharp questions.

## Recent News
- SIE reportedly partnered with Bad Robot Games to produce and publish the studio's first internally developed game, said to have been announced around December 4, 2025, though the exact announcement date couldn't be independently confirmed
- Ghost of Yōtei launched on PlayStation 5 on October 2, 2025 — this date is well confirmed — though framing it as a 'global storytelling milestone' reflects marketing language that hasn't been independently verified
- According to a Polygon year-in-review piece, Sony's two major 2025 first-party titles, Death Stranding 2: On the Beach and Ghost of Yōtei, together earned 14 Game Awards nominations but no wins — this specific tally hasn't been independently verified ([source](https://www.polygon.com/playstation-2025-sony-ps5-year-in-review))
- Unconfirmed reports suggest PlayStation launched a Family App in September 2025 aimed at simplifying family gaming experiences, though the exact launch month couldn't be verified
- One source indicates Sony evolved the PlayStation Store experience around an August 14, 2025 update, though this exact date remains unconfirmed
- SIE reportedly publishes an engineering blog (SIE.Blog) covering Company, Engineering, Impact, and Product topics, though the exact category names haven't been independently confirmed ([source](https://sonyinteractive.com/en/news/blog))
- A claimed August 2026 SIE blog post titled 'Turning Play into Progress: An Update on Sustainability Efforts' could not be verified and its future-dated timing raises some doubt
- A claimed July 2026 SIE blog post titled 'Level Up Your Summer: Online Safety Tips for Families on PlayStation' likewise could not be verified

## Funding & Business
- Sony Interactive Entertainment reportedly had FY25 revenue of approximately US$31.09 billion and operating income of about US$3.07 billion, with roughly 12,100 employees, though an independent check found revenue closer to $29.8B and the employee count unconfirmed ([source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Interactive_Entertainment))
- One source states that in Q2 FY2025, PlayStation's monthly active users grew 3% year-over-year to 119 million accounts with total play time up 1%, though these specific figures couldn't be independently confirmed ([source](https://www.sony.com/en/SonyInfo/IR/library/presen/er/pdf/25q2_sonyspeech.pdf))
- According to a Sony investor presentation, FY2025 (fiscal year ended March 31, 2026) results reportedly showed sales of 2,151.5 billion yen and operating income of 357.3 billion yen for the relevant segment, though which segment this refers to is unclear and the figures are unverified ([source](https://www.sony.com/en/SonyInfo/IR/library/presen/er/pdf/25q4_sonypre.pdf))
- Sony's Game & Network Services (G&NS) segment saw a 4% decrease in sales to 1,613.6 billion yen in Q3 FY2025, primarily due to lower PlayStation 5 hardware unit sales ([source](https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/sony-q3-fy2025-slides-22-operating-income-jump-prompts-forecast-upgrade-93CH-4486713))
- G&NS operating income reportedly increased 19% to 140.8 billion yen in Q3 FY2025, benefiting from foreign exchange rates, increased network services sales, and higher first-party game software sales, though the exact figure hasn't been independently confirmed ([source](https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/sony-q3-fy2025-slides-22-operating-income-jump-prompts-forecast-upgrade-93CH-4486713))
- PlayStation Monthly Active Users reportedly reached a record high of 132 million accounts in December, up 2% year-on-year, with total play time increasing 0.4% year-on-year for the quarter, though these specific growth rates remain unconfirmed ([source](https://www.sony.com/en/SonyInfo/IR/library/presen/er/pdf/25q3_sonyspeech.pdf))

## Tech Stack
- Per the job posting, the team's multi-platform application framework combines React Native, native platform integration, reusable UI components, SDK tooling, and developer documentation to help internal teams build PlayStation user experiences (from the job posting you provided)
- Per the job posting, this Software Engineer role requires working across JavaScript/TypeScript, native platform integration, C++, build systems, and SDK packaging to maintain and improve the framework (from the job posting you provided)
- A claimed December 2025 SIE engineering blog post by a Staff Software Engineer named Bahar Pattarkine reportedly discusses the challenges of launching new features across multiple hardware generations for the PlayStation Family App, though the author's title and exact publication date couldn't be confirmed ([source](https://sonyinteractive.com/en/news/blog/bridging-the-generational-gap-with-the-playstation-family-app))

## Role Context
- Per the job posting, SIE delivers hardware and network services to more than 100 million people as an entertainment leader; the posting describes these generically as 'network services' rather than naming PlayStation Network, Store, or Plus specifically (from the job posting you provided)
- Per the job posting, the role emphasizes improving SDK packaging, framework templates, sample apps, and documentation so partner application teams can adopt framework capabilities with less support, reflecting a strong internal developer-experience focus (from the job posting you provided)
- Unverified listings suggest SIE has other open software engineering roles, including an Associate Game Designer (Technical) and a Software Development Engineer in Test II Contractor position, potentially hybrid in Santa Monica, CA and San Mateo, CA — these specifics haven't been confirmed and don't appear in the job posting itself
- One aggregator listing points to an open Manager, Software Engineering position based in San Mateo, CA, though this specific role and location couldn't be verified
- According to CB Insights, SIE handles research and development, exhibition, and sales of hardware and software for the PlayStation platform, including PS5, PS4, PlayStation VR, PlayStation Store, and PlayStation Plus ([source](https://www.cbinsights.com/investor/sony-interactive-entertainment))
- CB Insights also notes that SIE was formerly known as Sony Computer Entertainment and is based in San Mateo, though this hasn't been independently confirmed elsewhere ([source](https://www.cbinsights.com/investor/sony-interactive-entertainment))
- An SIE research page reportedly estimates PlayStation Monthly Active Users at 125 million as of June 30, 2026, though this figure and its attribution remain unconfirmed ([source](https://sonyinteractive.com/en/our-company/business-data-sales))

## Culture
- Sony Interactive Entertainment holds an employee rating of 3.9 out of 5 stars based on 184 company reviews on Glassdoor ([source](https://www.glassdoor.com/Overview/Working-at-Sony-Interactive-Entertainment-EI_IE5580180.11,41.htm))
- Glassdoor reviews reportedly describe SIE as having a collaborative and inclusive atmosphere with a strong emphasis on teamwork and a fun work culture, though specific review wording couldn't be confirmed ([source](https://www.glassdoor.com/Reviews/Sony-Interactive-Entertainment-Reviews-E5580180.htm))
- Software Engineer reviews on Glassdoor reportedly mention decent work-life balance but note that some colleagues are not very technically advanced — specific review content is unconfirmed ([source](https://www.glassdoor.com/Reviews/Sony-Interactive-Entertainment-Software-Engineer-Reviews-EI_IE5580180.0,30_KO31,48.htm))
- A claimed March 2026 SIE blog post reportedly noted Sony Interactive marking 200 apprentices in its career program, though this figure and date couldn't be verified
- Employees in San Mateo, CA have reportedly given SIE a rating of 3.8 out of 5 stars based on 24 company reviews on Glassdoor, though the exact figures are unconfirmed ([source](https://www.glassdoor.com/Reviews/Sony-Interactive-Entertainment-San-Mateo-CA-Reviews-EI_IE5580180.0,30_IL.31,43_IC1147406.htm))
- One source suggests that 75% of SIE employees would recommend working there to a friend based on Glassdoor reviews, though this exact percentage is unconfirmed ([source](https://www.glassdoor.com/Reviews/Sony-Interactive-Entertainment-Reviews-E5580180.htm))
- A purported current Senior Software Engineer review from Aliso Viejo, CA (dated September 2026) describes SIE as having 'great culture and benefits' with 'good work life and balance,' while noting 'pay could be better' and a desire for more transparency — this quote and its details are unverified ([source](https://www.glassdoor.com/Reviews/Sony-Interactive-Entertainment-Reviews-E5580180.htm))
- According to anonymously submitted Glassdoor reviews, SIE employees reportedly rate compensation and benefits at 3.9 out of 5, though this figure appears drawn from a single review rather than an aggregate and couldn't be confirmed
- Sony's corporate strategy for PlayStation reportedly includes addressing player risks through online safety enhancements and moderation, and cultivating inclusivity within SIE and the gaming community through accessible functions in hardware and game development ([source](https://www.sony.com/en/SonyInfo/IR/library/corporatereport/CorporateReport2025_E.pdf))

## Talking Points
1. The role's focus on React Native plus native C++ integration aligns directly with the posting's described framework stack — worth highlighting any hands-on experience building SDKs, native modules, or cross-platform tooling that mirrors this exact combination.
2. With G&NS operating income reportedly up sharply in Q3 FY2025 partly due to network services growth, emphasizing your API design judgment and versioning discipline shows you understand how framework stability supports business-critical services at scale.
3. Given Glassdoor signals of decent work-life balance but mixed technical depth among some peers, positioning yourself as someone who raises the technical bar through rigorous code reviews and documentation could resonate with a team focused on developer-experience quality.
4. The emphasis in the posting on reducing partner-team support burden through better SDK packaging and sample apps is a great match if you can speak to past experience translating internal developer pain points into reusable framework improvements.
5. Since PlayStation's monthly active user base is reportedly in the 120-130 million range and growing, framing your work on backward compatibility and maintainable APIs as directly supporting a massive, active developer and player ecosystem shows business awareness.

## Questions to Ask Them
- How does the framework team balance shipping new features versus maintaining backward compatibility across the many internal application teams that depend on these APIs?
- Can you describe a recent example where feedback from an application team as a framework consumer led to a meaningful change in the SDK or framework architecture?
- Given the mix of JavaScript/TypeScript and native C++ work, how is the team structured — do engineers specialize in one layer or move fluidly across the full stack?
- What does the debugging workflow look like when an issue spans JavaScript, native code, and CI — are there established tools or is this often exploratory?
- How does the team think about versioning and deprecation for framework APIs that are consumed by many internal teams simultaneously?
